messages:
maria: quick sync — we rolled int8+kv-cache on a few small llama variants and the e2e evals show a subtle quality dip on long prompts. need to decide guardrails before wide rollout.

devin: can you share concrete failure patterns? repetition? wrong facts?

maria: mainly increased repetition and some formatting collapse on enumerated outputs. small but consistent on >1024 tokens.

ashwin: sounds like quant noise accumulating in the attention kv cache. int8 has lower SNR for slow-decaying attention weights. fp8 experiments earlier had fewer repeats but higher variance across seeds.

priya: what's the perf/cost delta we're chasing here? ballpark numbers help tradeoffs.

devin: int8 ~30% token-cost reduction vs fp16 baseline, fp8 ~40% but fp8 ops are less stable across kernels and sometimes cause mismatched logits. int4 can give ~55% but quality hit is larger.

maria: proposal: implement a "precision-selector" that picks profile per-request using simple heuristics + runtime telemetry and falls back to safer profile when risk > threshold. we need the shape of those heuristics.

ashwin: heuristics that seemed useful in experiments:
- long input length (>1k) => avoid int4
- high entropic prompts (open-ended creative) => prefer fp16/fp8 over int8
- requests with boundary tokens (tables/code) => prefer higher precision

priya: how do we detect "high entropic" in practice? cheap signal only.

devin: a few ideas: short token-level surprisal estimate using a lightweight ngram / compressed logits sketch, user-provided hint header like X-precision-hint, or observe prefix perplexity from a cached small model. all cheap-ish.

maria: we should also add an eval gating criterion: if per-profile eval score drop > 1% on our curated long-context suite, block rollout. we already have the eval harness but need per-request mapping.

eval-bot: new run complete: model=llama-13b, profile=int8, eval_suite=long-context-5120, quality_drop=1.4%, latency_change=-11%

ashwin: 1.4% is small but consistent. does it map to user-visible regressions? need sample triage.

priya: operationally, rollout plan: shadow int8 for 2w, track these signals per-route, do canary at 1% traffic, have automatic fallback to fp16 if seq_quality_drop > 0.8% for that route.

maria: agree. we also need a runtime API hook so runtime can annotate a request with "precision_risk_score" which controllers use for routing. minimal schema: {score:float, reason:str}.

devin: sample runtime snippet for the profile config we discussed:
```
precision_profile: {
  model: "llama-13b",
  preferred: ["int8", "fp8", "fp16"],
  fallback: "fp16",
  risk_threshold: 0.008,
  telemetry_signals: ["input_len", "prefix_perp", "user_hint"]
}
```

ashwin: also add a conservative kernel-level checksum after kv-cache writes to detect silent corruption; if checksum mismatch, force fallback and mark metric. cheap guard.

priya: good call. add a chord in rollout dashboard to show per-route: cost delta, quality_drop, fallback_rate, and sample examples when quality_drop > 0.5%.

maria: action items: ashwin -> implement risk_score + kv-checksum shim (prio high), devin -> run 10k-sample shadow evaluation across top 20 routes, priya -> update rollout policy docs + dashboard tile. will reconvene next Tues.

deploy-bot: canary job created for route=search-autocomplete, config=precision_selector_v1, id=canary-197234-1 :rocket:

maria: thanks — please post initial numbers to #eng-ml when canary has 24h of traffic. :thumbsup:
